name: Arcticodactylus
isnote: Formerly a species of Eudimorphodon; placed in Eudimorphodontidae by some, but the relationships of Triassic pterosaurs are unstable, so it is placed here directly under Pterosauria.
sum: The smallest known pterosaur, from the Late Triassic of East Greenland.
wsnote: Estimated 24 cm for the holotype individual.
holotype: MGUH VP 3393 — Ørsted Dal Member, Fleming Fjord Formation (Norian–Rhaetian), East Greenland.
biology: Multi-cusped teeth (three to five points), fewer than in any other Triassic pterosaur; likely took small invertebrates.
author: Kellner 2015

species.name: Arcticodactylus cromptonellus
species.author: (Jenkins et al. 2001)
species.ref: F. A. Jenkins, N. H. Shubin, and S. M. Gatesy, K. Padian. 2001. A diminutive pterosaur (Pterosauria: Eudimorphodontidae) from the Greenlandic Triassic. Bulletin Museum of Comparative Zoology 156(1):151-170

sources.text: A. W. A. Kellner. 2015. Comments on Triassic pterosaurs with discussion about ontogeny and description of new taxa. Anais da Academia Brasileira de Ciências 87(2):669-689
